thread:
maria.gomez: Quick heads-up — I kicked off a surface scan against our latest GPU node image (dedicated + private bundles). vuln-bot picked up a few driver/CUDA related CVEs and some outdated NCCL builds.

vuln-bot: Automated scan results: 6 findings (3 high, 2 medium, 1 low). Notable: CVE-2026-0456 (NVidia driver privilege escalation, reported for r550+), CVE-2026-0472 (cuDNN info leak on cudnn < 9.0.2), and NCCL lib path symlink perms (low). Full report: https://vuln.internal/reports/1766120050

kevin.li: Can you paste the driver versions and which images are affected? we have multiple channels: hosted-prod, dedicated-2026q1, private-vpc-archived.

maria.gomez: Affected: nvidia-driver 550.102.04 on images: dedicated-2026q1-base, private-vpc-2201. CUDA runtimes: 12.1.0 and 11.8 on different images. cuDNN: 8.9.x on some, 9.0.0-rc on others. NCCL: 2.14.3 and 2.9.6 variants.

raj.patel: Exploitability note: CVE-2026-0456 requires local unprivileged container escape vector + sysfs write privileges — higher risk in dedicated pools where customers can run untrusted containers. For hosted API it's lower since we control runtime sandboxing.

elaine.chen: +1 to prioritize dedicated and private pools. We should also validate KMS-signed driver policy; if we can enforce kernel module signing via our KMS/HSM, that reduces attack surface for driver tampering.

kevin.li: For compatibility: if we bump driver to patched 551.x we need to validate CUDA 12.1 + cuDNN 9 matrix. Rolling upgrade could break some pinned model images. Suggest matrix test: driver 551 + CUDA 12.1/11.8 + cuDNN 8.9/9.0 + NCCL 2.14/2.9. I'll draft a test matrix.

maria.gomez: Proposal: triage steps -> 1) reproduce PoC in isolated lab node, 2) check exploitability in containerized environment, 3) run compatibility smoke matrix, 4) patch canary pool then full rollout with automatic fallback.

ops-oncall: For rollout: canary in non-prod dedicated pool (c1), monitor for kernel oops, cuda-runtime failures, and model perf regressions for 48h. Canary config: 10 nodes, daily bursts enabled. If >2 nodes show GPU driver reboots or CUDA init failures -> rollback.

vuln-bot: CVSS scores: CVE-2026-0456: 7.8 (High, Priv Esc), CVE-2026-0472: 6.4 (Medium, Info Leak). Suggested ETA to patch: 72 hours for dedicated, 7 days for hosted non-critical.

raj.patel: Workarounds: restrict CAP_SYS_ADMIN in container profiles, enforce no-new-privs, mount sysfs ro where possible, and ensure driver package is signed. We should also add an audit rule for module load events (auditd/ebpf).

elaine.chen: Action items: @kevin.li create compatibility test matrix and schedule run, @maria.gomez repro & PoC in lab, @raj.patel provide mitigation config snippets for kiosk container profiles, ops-oncall to prepare canary nodes and rollback playbook.

kevin.li: I'll add tests to CI: quick smoke (basic cudaInit + small model inference) + perf check (latency spike detection). Will output results to /ci/gpu-compat/1766120050.

maria.gomez: PoC notes (initial): reproduced privilege escalation inside privileged container with SYS_ADMIN granted. Minimal steps: 
```
# repro snippet (lab only)
docker run --cap-add=SYS_ADMIN --security-opt seccomp=unconfined -it gpu-toolbox:lab bash
# trigger: write to /sys/module/nvidia/parameters/something
```
Observations: host kernel module loading allowed; signed modules prevented exploit.

raj.patel: Here's a short mitigation config for runtime (paste into AMI bake + runtime profiles): 
```
# runtime profile snippet
container_runtime:
  no_new_privs: true
  capabilities:
    drop: ["SYS_ADMIN", "NET_ADMIN"]
mounts:
  - { path: "/sys", options: ["ro"] }
```

ops-oncall: I'll stage canary nodes tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Need final patch package and signed driver by then. Who owns packaging?

elaine.chen: Security will sign drivers via our KMS integration (I’ll coordinate with infra team). We need build artifact naming convention to tie to KMS signed digest and release notes.

maria.gomez: Prioritization decision: escalate CVE-2026-0456 to P0 for dedicated/private rollout. CVE-2026-0472 P1. Low-risk NCCL perms P2. Timeline: patch and canary deploy within 72h, rollback window 48h, full rollout after 7 days if no issues.

kevin.li: Noted. I'll start matrix today. tagging this thread to track progress.

elaine.chen: I'll open an internal vendor ticket with NVIDIA for driver 551.x patch details and request signed binaries for our KMS pipeline.

maria.gomez: Thanks all. I'll update the incident tracker and add the mitigation checklist. Short next check-in at 12:30 UTC. :thumbsup:
